description: Policy routing of the router: rules that send the forwarded traffic they match, coming in on a zone's links, on interfaces or on any link, to a VRF's routing table, another table or a next hop, whatever its destination's route. The first rule that matches decides; documents apply in the order of their names.

interfaces.description: Interfaces the traffic comes in on, by name or glob, a glob being a prefix followed by `*`; excludes `zone`.

zone.description: FirewallZone whose links the traffic comes in on; excludes `interfaces`.

in.description: Where the traffic comes in: a zone or interfaces; null for every link.

rules.description: Rules in order: the first that matches a packet decides where it goes.

match.description: What the rule matches, at least one term: a rule for every packet says so, such as with `source: {cidrs: [0.0.0.0/0]}`.

cidrs.description: Address ranges that match; excludes `set`. In each family the rule matches the ranges of that family.

destination.description: Destination addresses: the ranges of an AddressSet in `set`, or address ranges in `cidrs`; null matches every destination.

destinationPorts.description: Destination ports, each a port or a range `<first>-<last>`, with the protocol `tcp`, `udp` or `sctp`; empty matches every port.

dscp.description: DSCP values of the packets, each from 0 to 63; empty matches every value.

family.description: Address family the rule matches; null matches each family its protocol and addresses leave.

protocol.description: Protocol the rule matches; null matches every protocol. `icmp` is IPv4's and `icmpv6` IPv6's.

cidrs.description: Address ranges that match; excludes `set`. In each family the rule matches the ranges of that family.

source.description: Source addresses: the ranges of an AddressSet in `set`, or address ranges in `cidrs`; null matches every source.

sourcePorts.description: Source ports, each a port or a range `<first>-<last>`, with the protocol `tcp`, `udp` or `sctp`; empty matches every port.

to.description: Where the traffic the rule matches goes: `vrf`, `table` or `nextHop`.

address.description: Address of the router the traffic leaves through, of the family the rule matches.

interface.description: Link the next hop is on, which a Network document names alone in its `[Match]` section; the route goes into that Network.

table.description: Routing table of the next hop: a default route through it and an unreachable default route after it, so that the traffic is dropped while the link is down. It is none of 253, 254 and 255 and no VRF's table. No other next hop and no rule's `table` may name it either, which the outputs check when they render the config, at an apply or a `--dry-run`, and `chalkctl validate` does not.

nextHop.description: Router the traffic leaves through, by the default route of a table of its own; excludes `vrf` and `table`.

table.description: Routing table that routes the traffic, by number: 254 is the main table. Not 255, the kernel's local table, and no VRF's table, which `vrf` names. A destination the table has no route to takes the route it would take without the policy; excludes `vrf` and `nextHop`.

vrf.description: VRF document whose routing table routes the traffic; excludes `table` and `nextHop`.
